summary: Iteration 5 — focused retest of the 3 iteration-4 ArchiveScene defects + the the-s/giant collision, plus the requested spot-checks and regression sweep. Method: hard reload per viewport, pin base read dynamically from the GSAP pin-spacer (1920x800=20960, 1920x1080=28296, 390x844=22114), window.__lenis.scrollTo(y,{immediate:true}) + 1.9s settle, t = d*23.3 desktop / d*13.25 mobile, span 11.5*innerHeight desktop / 6.8*innerHeight mobile, effective-opacity probe (ancestor opacity/visibility/display) plus bounding boxes and raw transform matrices. RESULT: RETEST 1, 2, 3 and the desktop spot-checks all PASS. RETEST 4 (mobile) partially FAILS: mid-sequence ARCHIVE clipping is correct, but .ax-beg (BEGINNING.) and .ax-just (IS JUST) lose their horizontal centering on mobile — their boxes start at left=195px (left:50%) with transform tx=0, so they run off the right edge and are cut in half in the IS JUST beat (t~7.5), the BEGINNING. beat (t~8.6) and the final mobile resolve (t~12.0). Screenshot-confirmed at 390x844 (only 'IS JUS' / 'BEGIN' visible). Regression green: pytest 9/9, nav-process/nav-capabilities/nav-contact anchors scroll, nav-start -> /start renders the configurator, zero console errors at every viewport (not even the benign 'scale not eligible for reset' warning fired this run).

ui_bugs.issue: On mobile both elements render from left:50% without the -translate-x-1/2 offset, so they overflow the right edge and are clipped. Measured at 390x844: t=7.5 .ax-just box x=(196..524) cx=360 (should be 195) op=1; t=8.6 .ax-beg box x=(195..558) cx=376 op=0.29; t=12.0 final resolve .ax-just x=(310..409) cx=360, .ax-beg x=(231..522) cx=376 — while .ax-arch3 (no GSAP x/y set) is correctly centered at cx=195. Raw matrices show tx=0 for .ax-just/.ax-beg (e.g. matrix(0.3,0,0,0.3,0,-50.9)) vs tx=-135.9 (=-50%) for .ax-arch3, i.e. the GSAP sets on x/y overwrote the Tailwind percentage translate. So 'THE ARCHIVE / IS JUST / BEGINNING. stacked cleanly' is NOT satisfied on mobile (vertical order is right: 203-249 / 407-437 / 596-653, horizontal is broken). Fix: add xPercent:-50, yPercent:-50 explicitly in the mobile tl.set() calls for .ax-beg and .ax-just (desktop keeps centering: .ax-beg cx=960 at d=0.95).

action_items: Mobile only: restore horizontal centering for .ax-beg and .ax-just (add xPercent:-50 / yPercent:-50 to the mobile GSAP sets) — IS JUST beat, BEGINNING. beat and the final mobile resolve are all clipped off the right edge at 390x844.
critical_code_review_comments: ArchiveScene relies on Tailwind's -translate-x-1/2/-translate-y-1/2 for centering while GSAP also writes x/y on the same elements; that mix is what silently broke mobile centering. Set xPercent/yPercent in GSAP for every element GSAP moves and drop the translate utility classes on those nodes.

Mobile timeline still reuses .ax-just for the final resolve (desktop now uses the dedicated .ax-just2). Consider mirroring the desktop split so the mobile resolve does not inherit the beat-H transform state.

rca_of_the_issue: GSAP parses the element's existing computed transform when it first writes x/y. On the mobile timeline .ax-beg (tl.set x:'0vw', y:'0vh' at 0, then y/scale sets at 10.9/11.25) and .ax-just (tl.set x:'0vw', scale:0.3 at 11.6, plus the fromTo x:105vw->0vw at 7.0) end up with translate tx=0 instead of the -50% supplied by the Tailwind -translate-x-1/2 class, so both are positioned from left:50% and overflow the right edge. Elements GSAP never moves horizontally (.ax-arch3, .ax-arch2) keep the -50% and stay centered, which is why only these two are broken and only on mobile.
